text:
sara: FYI ran into a nasty teardown error when using the Python SDK Async client from a module-scoped pytest fixture with pytest-asyncio + uvloop. Repro is a session-scoped fixture that creates the client once, yields it to tests, and then awaits client.aclose() in teardown.

sara: minimal fixture:
```py
import pytest
from redwood import AsyncClient

@pytest.fixture(scope=\"session\")
def sdk_client():
    client = AsyncClient()  # created at import/session time
    yield client
    asyncio.get_event_loop().run_until_complete(client.aclose())
```

sara: symptoms: tests pass, but CI job sometimes hangs on shutdown or throws \"RuntimeError: Event loop is closed\" from httpcore when client.aclose() runs, stack shows httpcore trying to schedule on a loop that was already closed by pytest-asyncio plugin.

mike: yep this smells like mixing sync loop management with async fixtures. session-scoped fixtures run across multiple event loop instances in pytest-asyncio if tests use different plugin policies, and calling run_until_complete against a closed loop is dicey.

rachel: two things to consider: 1) don't create AsyncClient at import/session level on the sync path, 2) use an async fixture so teardown runs in the running loop. Example async fixture:
```py
@pytest.fixture(scope=\"session\")
async def sdk_client():
    client = AsyncClient()
    yield client
    await client.aclose()
```

rachel: that ensures aclose() runs on the same loop used by tests. Also avoids trying to call asyncio.get_event_loop() which can return a loop that's already closed.

sara: switching to async fixture fixed the teardown error for me locally, but I hit mypy/typing errors: AsyncClient is both an async context manager and has .aclose() coroutine; mypy complains if the type isn't annotated correctly in fixture return type. Any typing suggestions?

mike: annotate the fixture return type as AsyncClient (the class), but if you need the protocol for typing tools, addfrom typing import AsyncContextManager; annotate as AsyncContextManager[AsyncClient] if you yield an async context. Alternatively annotate as AsyncClient and ignore mypy for the fixture if it's noisy.

rachel: also consider exposing an async factory in the SDK: async def create_async_client(...) -> AsyncClient. That makes it explicit that creation may do async work (e.g., warmup). It also avoids surprises where class constructor looks sync but binds transport objects to current loop.

sara: another wrinkle: tests that use anyio (pytest-anyio) work differently than pytest-asyncio. Some CI jobs use anyio backend for trio tests and we saw \"Task got Future attached to a different loop\" when test used trio backend. We might need to document supported test backends or design the client to be backend-agnostic (lazy per-loop or no loop-affine resources).

mike: for a robust SDK we should: 1) avoid creating httpx.AsyncClient in __init__, 2) provide an async factory or async context manager, 3) implement per-loop cache keyed by asyncio.get_running_loop() or id, 4) provide sync wrapper helpers for sync users. Also add a note about test fixture scopes (session/module) and async teardown.

sara: opened GH issue with repro and CI logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/2402 — includes mypy details and a minimal tox/pytest config that reproduces the hang.

ci-bot: Created issue #2402 (redwood-inference/python-sdk): \"pytest fixture session-scope + AsyncClient teardown causes closed loop/hang on CI\" assigned to @mike. :white_check_mark:

mike: will pair on this. plan: submit a small fix to switch to lazy creation + async factory and add pytest matrix job that runs pytest-asyncio and anyio with uvloop to catch regressions. Add tests for session/module fixtures.

rachel: also add a docs blurb under testing.md: \"Do not instantiate AsyncClient at import time; prefer async fixtures or async factories. Examples for pytest-asyncio and pytest-anyio included.\"

sara: thanks all, reduced our CI flakes by switching to async fixture in the short term. Will link PR when ready.
